    Sectional paths #

    Proof of Proposition 4.1, Step 1: "A path is sectional if it contains no consecutive pair (σa)a. A sectional path cannot occur as a monomial term in a contextual mesh relation. Its coefficient therefore defines a linear functional annihilating the mesh ideal, and the path is nonzero in the mesh category. Since the mesh category is finite-dimensional, there is an integer N such that all paths of length at least N vanish. Hence every sectional path has length less than N."

    A path is recorded by its list of arrows (arrowList), and it is sectional when no two consecutive arrows form a mesh pair (σ a, a).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
